title: zingbus Plus vs Maxx: Which Bus Service to Choose
summary: A clear zingbus Plus vs Maxx comparison of comfort, meals, price and onboard service, so you can pick the right bus for your next intercity trip.
body_markdown:
Two people booking the same overnight route often end up on very different buses. One picks the option that costs less and still gets a comfortable sleeper. The other pays more for a flat bed, a hot meal and a calmer cabin. That decision usually comes down to the gap between zingbus Plus and zingbus Maxx.


## **What Sets the Two Services Apart**


This guide compares the two on the things that actually shape an overnight trip: comfort, sleep quality, meals, onboard facilities, service and price. It draws on verified zingbus product details instead of brochure language, so every difference here reflects what you genuinely receive.


zingbus Plus is the widely available sleeper tier that runs across a large route network, while the[zingbus Maxx service](https://www.zingbus.com/blog/zingbus-maxx-review-worth-it/) sits at the premium end. Knowing what each one leads to helps you match the bus to both the journey and the budget you have in mind.


# **zingbus Plus vs Maxx: A Practical Comparison for Your Next Trip**


Both services run through the same booking app, the same live tracking and the same core safety systems. The real gap is about comfort, food and how much you pay for the upgrade. The sections below break down each difference so the choice becomes clear rather than a guess.


## **What zingbus Plus Covers**


zingbus Plus is the mid tier sleeper service. It runs AC sleeper and seater coaches that vary by corridor, so the exact bus depends on the route you book. On longer overnight routes you get reclining berths, air conditioning, charging points and, on select services, an onboard washroom.


Meals on Plus are not built into the fare. On many routes you can pre book the Food on Bus meal service during checkout, and on three specific routes, Delhi to Lucknow, Delhi to Gorakhpur and Chennai to Coimbatore, a Freemeal coupon applies to Plus buses. The strength of Plus is reach, since it serves far more destinations than the premium fleet.


## **What zingbus Maxx Covers**


zingbus Maxx is the premium service, built on the Volvo B8R 9600 coach. Its berths open to a full 180 degree flat sleeping position, which is the single biggest comfort difference on an overnight run. Each berth has a personal entertainment screen, USB and Type-C charging and a personal reading light.


The fare includes a five course meal served at your berth by the Gold Star Crew, so there is no meal to add at checkout. Maxx buses carry an onboard bio washroom and individual climate control, and the service records a 90.5% CSAT across its routes, with 40% of women travellers returning as repeat passengers.


## **zingbus Plus vs Maxx at a Glance**


The table below sets the two services next to each other on the points travellers ask about most, so you can scan the differences before reading the detail underneath. Treat it as a quick reference, not the full picture.


**Feature** **zingbus Plus** **zingbus Maxx**


Coach AC sleeper or seater, varies by route Volvo B8R 9600


Berth Reclining sleeper 180 degree flat berth

Crew Driver and conductor Gold Star Crew service


Route reach Wide network Selected premium routes


## **The Price Difference and What You Pay For**


The price difference between the two is real, and it buys specific things rather than a vague sense of luxury. With Maxx you are paying for the flat berth, the included five course meal, the trained crew and the bio washroom. With Plus you keep more of your money and still travel on a comfortable AC sleeper.


Fares on both services move with the route, the season and how early you book, so the gap on a quiet weekday looks different from the gap during a festival rush. Rather than quote a figure that dates quickly, it is better to open the route on the zingbus app and read the live fare for each option side by side. Prices are approximate and may vary based on season, demand, and availability.


## **Comfort and Sleep Quality**


This is where the two services separate most clearly. A reclining Plus berth is comfortable for a night, but it holds a slight incline. The Maxx berth lies fully flat, which changes how well you actually sleep on a long overnight leg, especially if you are tall or a light sleeper.


Individual climate control on Maxx also means you are not sharing one temperature setting with the whole coach. On a hill route where nights turn cold, that control is worth more than it sounds. For a short evening hop, the difference matters far less, and Plus is usually enough.


## **Meals: Where the Two Genuinely Differ**


Food is one of the most misunderstood parts of this comparison, so it is worth stating plainly. The Maxx meal is a five course spread included in the ticket and served at your berth by the Gold Star Crew. It is part of the fare, and you do not order it separately.


Plus works differently. There is no meal built into the fare. On many Plus routes you can add the Food on Bus service, a pre booked selection of twelve vegetarian items ordered at checkout or through My Trip and handed to you at your seat by the onboard marshal. Freemeal is separate again and applies only to Plus buses on Delhi to Lucknow, Delhi to Gorakhpur and Chennai to Coimbatore. The Maxx meal and Food on Bus are not the same thing.


## **Onboard Experience and Service**


The customer experience on Maxx leans on the Gold Star Crew, who go beyond the usual driver and conductor. That staffing, along with the flat berths and included meal, is what pushes the 90.5% CSAT figure and the 40% repeat rate among women travellers on the service.


Plus does not carry that dedicated crew, but it shares the safety backbone that runs across zingbus. Both services include CCTV on the bus, GPS live tracking through the app, verified drivers with background checks, female friendly seating and a two driver rotation on routes that run beyond six hours. The base standard is the same, and the extras are what you are choosing between.


## **Which One Is Better for Which Traveller**


There is no single winner here, because the better service depends on the trip. If you travel often, watch the budget, or take shorter evening routes, zingbus Plus usually makes more sense and reaches more places. If the journey is a long overnight one and sleep matters, Maxx earns its higher fare.


It also helps to check availability before deciding, since Maxx runs on selected premium corridors rather than the full network. On a route where only Plus runs, the comparison is settled for you. Where both are offered, the choice is simply how much comfort you want to pay for on that particular night.


## **Making the Call**


The honest summary is that neither service is trying to be the other. zingbus Plus is the practical, wide reaching sleeper for everyday intercity travel, and it handles most trips well. Maxx is the option you pick when the journey is long, the night matters, or you simply want to arrive rested.


Before you book, open your route on the zingbus app and look at both fares and the amenities listed for that specific service and date. The right answer changes by route and by season, and the live listing tells you what is actually running the night you plan to travel.


## **zingbus Plus vs Maxx: Common Questions**


The questions below cover what most travellers check before choosing between the two services.


### **What is the main difference between zingbus Plus and Maxx?**


The zingbus Plus vs Maxx difference is comfort and inclusions. Plus is a mid tier AC sleeper, while Maxx adds flat berths, an included meal and a trained crew.


### **Is there a big price difference between the two services?**


Yes, Maxx costs more than Plus because the fare includes flat berths, a five course meal and the Gold Star Crew. The exact gap changes by route and season.


### **Which service is better for an overnight journey?**


For a long overnight journey, Maxx is usually better because its 180 degree flat berths let you sleep properly, while Plus suits shorter routes and tighter budgets well.


### **Does zingbus Maxx include meals?**


Yes, zingbus Maxx includes a five course meal in the ticket price, served at your berth by the Gold Star Crew, so you do not order food separately.


### **Do zingbus Plus buses include free meals?**


Plus buses do not include meals by default. You can add the paid Food on Bus service on many routes, and a Freemeal coupon applies on three specific routes only.


### **Do both services have an onboard washroom?**


Maxx carries an onboard bio washroom as standard. On zingbus Plus, an onboard washroom is available on select longer routes rather than across the entire network.


### **Are zingbus Plus and Maxx available on every route?**


No, Plus runs across a wide network, while Maxx operates on selected premium corridors. Check your specific route on the app to see which service is running.


### **Which has a better customer experience?**


Maxx records a 90.5% CSAT and a 40% repeat rate among women travellers, helped by its crew and comfort. Plus offers a solid, more widely available standard.


### **Do both buses have live tracking and safety features?**


Yes, both include GPS live tracking through the app, CCTV, verified drivers, female friendly seating and a two driver rotation on routes longer than six hours.


### **Can I charge my phone on both services?**


Both services offer charging. Maxx provides USB and Type-C charging with a personal reading light at each berth, while Plus buses carry charging points that vary by coach.


### **Is zingbus Maxx worth the extra cost?**


Maxx is worth it when the trip is a long overnight one and rest matters, since the flat berth and included meal justify the fare. For short hops, Plus is enough.


### **How do I check the current fare for each service?**


Open your route and date in the zingbus app and compare the live fares and listed amenities for Plus and Maxx side by side before booking your seat.
